pos.personaBrief: Chelsea 2016/17 not a team that wants the ball (Bola na Rede) and Inter's possession fell from 61% to 45% in the winning run while they hit on the break (Sky, Serie A analysis); Conte stresses balance.

pro.personaBrief: Chelsea went long (StatsBomb, Sky) and aimed at fast vertical play, but Inter built from the back via Brozovic/Eriksen and De Vrij/Bastoni carries.

est.personaBrief: Rehearsed 3-4-3/3-5-2 with fixed roles and wing-backs staying wide, a drilled positional structure, with Lukaku dropping to link.

lar.personaBrief: Attacks through wing-backs (Alonso, Moses, Young) with crosses to strikers, no true wingers, three central midfielders.

blo.personaBrief: Compact mid-block 5-3-2 with selective pressing and slowed reaction to loss (Bola na Rede), strikers pressing at times (Sky 'Go, go, go').

mar.personaBrief: Man-oriented, chain-reaction marking with defenders stepping out onto the ball carrier; Chelsea centrals leaving the line to follow.

pla.personaBrief: Imposes his 3-back system and ruthlessly cleared players who did not fit (Icardi, Perisic, Nainggolan), but changed shape after the Arsenal defeat and tunes to opponents.

res.personaBrief: Pragmatic, balance first, won titles by solidity and counters; shifted back to a pragmatic strategy at Inter.

sis.personaBrief: Drilled system with duties for all; dropped Terry, Ivanovic and Costa feud shows no exemptions.

jog.personaBrief: Intense, physical teams: Kante's tackles, Lukaku as target, wing-backs running; but also values technical Eriksen/Brozovic.

bas.personaBrief: Wants older, title-winning professionals (Inter signings), though at Chelsea lowered average age somewhat with Christensen, Bakayoko.

lid.personaBrief: Frank, authoritarian boss who benched Terry and Ivanovic and fought Costa; stars follow the same rules.
